observations: In this run we observed the agent read the whole program at the start of every later session (ck2 step 2.2, ck4 steps 4.2-4.3, ck5 steps 5.2-5.3, ck6 steps 6.3-6.4) before editing, and add new modules for new commands (invention.py ck2, planner.py/build_string.py ck4, stock_list.py ck6). It refactored within planner.py twice: extracting _consume/_job_rows (ck5 diff line 213) and _invent (ck6 diff line 165). One copy appeared: invention_report.py repeats report.py's header lines (ck2). Verification was mainly running the CLI on spec examples (ck2 step 2.20 'ALL MATCH', ck5 step 5.8) plus regression spot-checks (ck3 step 3.6, ck6 step 6.10). In ck2 it fitted the probability formula to the spec numbers with /tmp scripts (steps 2.6-2.9). Most failures trace to spec readings: 'science' skills limited to the Science group (ck2 step 2.13), waste measured from ME 0 (ck3), and a strict split boundary the agent chose from conflicting spec text and examples, which it recorded in a memory note (ck5 step 5.13); that note was gone in ck6 (step 6.2 ERROR). In ck6 the agent reported a spec-example mismatch (Nitrogen Fuel Block 34 vs 35) and left it (step 6.11).
